summary:
The Halting the Epidemic of Addiction and Loss Act of 2025 would require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to ensure that Department of Health and Human Services regulations and guidance for specified opioid-related grant programs do not treat references to opioid overdose reversal drugs as limited to naloxone.

Section 2(a) establishes a prospective directive applicable whenever HHS issues a regulation or guidance for any grant program addressing opioid misuse and use disorders. As appropriate, any reference in such regulation or guidance to an opioid overdose reversal drug, including a reference to naloxone, must be inclusive of any opioid overdose reversal drug approved under section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, 21 U.S.C. 355, for emergency treatment of a known or suspected opioid overdose.

Section 2(b) imposes a retrospective updating requirement. Not later than one year after enactment, the Secretary must update covered pre-enactment references to opioid overdose reversal drugs, including naloxone, so that they are inclusive of any opioid overdose reversal drug that has been approved or otherwise authorized for use by the Food and Drug Administration. Covered references are limited to references in HHS regulations or guidance issued before enactment and included in either: the grant program for State and Tribal response to opioid use disorders under section 1003 of the 21st Century Cures Act, 42 U.S.C. 290ee-3a, commonly referred to as State Opioid Response Grants and Tribal Opioid Response Grants; or the grant program for priority substance use disorder prevention needs of regional and national significance under section 516 of the Public Health Service Act, 42 U.S.C. 290bb-22.

The bill does not amend the text of the cited statutes, create a new grant program, authorize appropriations, or appropriate funds.
